fixes.explanation: Good guess, friend, and I'll admit "home" sounds right. But the verse says he flees "To save one’s own life…" (Deuteronomy 4:42). The word is life, not home. The text doesn't say where he was when he started running, and it doesn't say what happens to the house. Home I could bake a new one out of dough, but life is the thing on the line here.

That's right, baker, and look at that lineup. Bezer belongs to the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead to the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan to the Manassites (Deuteronomy 4:43). Three cities, three tribes, and nobody had to share a cookie box. Moses names them one by one, and each one has a tribe's name on it.

A king of Moab? Friend, I looked all over that verse and he never shows up! Moses names three cities, and each one belongs to a tribe: Bezer to the Reubenites, Ramoth to the Gadites, Golan to the Manassites (Deuteronomy 4:43). No king, no crown, no royal oven. I almost wish he was in there, though, because that would've been a wild twist.
